The test image shows a tomato/pepper plant with:
- Broad, heart-shaped leaves
- Marginal yellowing/chlorosis
- Small whitish spots visible on some leaves (lower-left)
- Possible mosaic-like mottling pattern (light/dark green patches)

Top candidates: Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus, Powdery_Mildew, Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus. Starting with CMV reference.
CMV reference shows severely distorted, narrow leaves — doesn't match the broad leaves in test image. Checking Powdery Mildew next.
Powdery mildew shows distinct white powdery patches — the test image spots are more yellowish/small, not powdery. Checking Bacterial Speck.
Bacterial speck shows dark/black spots with yellow halos — test image doesn't match that. Checking Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus.

TSWV shows severely wilted, dark necrotic plants — doesn't match. The test image has relatively intact broad leaves with pale patches and marginal yellowing. Checking Leaf Mold and Bacterial Canker next.
Bacterial canker shows extensive brown marginal necrosis — too severe for test image. I've used 6 views. Need 2 more covering new classes. Checking Bacterial Wilt and a second Leaf Mold reference.
Bacterial Wilt reference shows a diagnostic stem test (ooze), not helpful for visual comparison. Using my last view on Phytophthora Blight.

Now I have 8 views complete. Let me assess:

| CMV (Bugwood_1) | No — severely distorted narrow leaves |
| Powdery Mildew (CDDM_116) | Possible — white spots, but test image less powdery |
| Bacterial Speck (Bugwood_14) | No — dark spots with yellow halos |
| TSWV (Bugwood_3) | No — severe necrotic wilting |
| Leaf Mold (CDDM_313) | Partial — pale blotches on leaf surface |
| Bacterial Canker (Bugwood_1) | No — severe brown marginal necrosis |
| Bacterial Wilt (Bugwood_3) | Not comparable (diagnostic stem test) |
| Phytophthora Blight (Bugwood_21) | **Strong leaf-shape match** — same broad, heart-shaped pepper-type leaves; left-side plant shows small whitish spots and marginal yellowing nearly identical to test image |

**Key decision:** The Phytophthora Blight reference (Bugwood_21) contained a pepper plant on its left side with identical broad, heart-shaped leaf morphology to the test image. The small whitish/pale spots and marginal yellowing in the test image correspond to early-stage water-soaked lesions consistent with Phytophthora Blight. No other reference matched the host plant leaf shape this closely.
